subject: ela
cluster: Range of reading and level of text complexity
intro: Read each informational passage carefully, then choose the single best answer based only on what the passage says.

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

Sea otters spend almost their whole lives in the water. To keep from drifting apart while they sleep, they often hold hands with one another, floating together in a group. They also wrap themselves in long strands of kelp, which act like an anchor and keep the current from carrying them out to sea.

According to the passage, why do sea otters wrap themselves in kelp?
A) To keep warm in cold ocean water
B) To keep the current from carrying them out to sea
C) To hide from larger ocean animals
D) To gather food for later
items.answer: B) To keep the current from carrying them out to sea

steps: The question asks for an explicit detail stated in the passage.
The text says the kelp acts like an anchor and keeps the current from carrying the otters out to sea, which matches choice B.
Choice A (warmth) sounds reasonable from prior knowledge but is never stated in the passage.
Choice C (hiding) and choice D (gathering food) are not mentioned anywhere in the text.
solution.answer: B) To keep the current from carrying them out to sea

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

The camel is well suited for life in the desert. Its hump does not hold water, as many people think. Instead, the hump stores fat, which the camel's body can break down for energy when food is scarce. A camel can travel for days across the sand with little to eat.

According to the passage, what does a camel's hump store?
A) Water for the dry season
B) Sand it has swallowed
C) Fat the body can use for energy
D) Food it saves to eat later
items.answer: C) Fat the body can use for energy

steps: The passage directly states that the hump stores fat, which the camel's body breaks down for energy.
Choice C restates this fact, so it is correct.
Choice A is the common belief the passage corrects; the text says the hump does NOT hold water.
Choices B and D are not supported anywhere in the passage.
solution.answer: C) Fat the body can use for energy

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

Many plants in the desert have learned to be dormant during the hottest months. A dormant plant slows down and almost stops growing, waiting until cooler, wetter weather returns. Then it springs back to life and grows quickly.

What does the word "dormant" mean as it is used in this passage?
A) Growing very quickly
B) In a resting, slowed-down state
C) Completely dead
D) A type of desert flower
items.answer: B) In a resting, slowed-down state

steps: Use the context clues around the word to find its meaning.
The passage explains that a dormant plant slows down, almost stops growing, and waits for better weather, which matches choice B.
Choice A is the opposite; growing quickly is what the plant does later, after it is no longer dormant.
Choice C is wrong because the plant springs back to life, so it is not dead.
Choice D guesses a meaning from the way the word looks rather than using the context, which is a common error.
solution.answer: B) In a resting, slowed-down state

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

Libraries today do far more than lend books. Many offer free internet access to people who cannot afford it at home. They host story hours for young children and homework help for older students. Some lend tools, musical instruments, or even cooking equipment. Others run classes that teach adults new job skills. For families with little money, the local library can be one of the most useful places in a whole community.

Which sentence best states the central idea of the passage?
A) Libraries lend tools, instruments, and cooking equipment.
B) Libraries offer free internet to people who lack it at home.
C) Modern libraries provide many valuable services beyond lending books.
D) Libraries host story hours for young children.
items.answer: C) Modern libraries provide many valuable services beyond lending books.

steps: The central idea is the main point that the whole passage develops, not one example from it.
Every sentence gives a different service libraries offer, and the passage opens by saying libraries do far more than lend books, so choice C captures the whole point.
Choices A, B, and D are each true supporting details, but they each name only one service and are too narrow to be the central idea.
Choosing one vivid detail instead of the overall point is a common mistake when finding the central idea.
solution.answer: C) Modern libraries provide many valuable services beyond lending books.

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

In 1271, a young man named Marco Polo left Italy with his father and uncle to travel east. After three and a half years of hard travel, they reached the court of the emperor of China. Marco spent the next seventeen years exploring the empire. When he finally returned home in 1295, few people believed his stories of the riches he had seen.

How are the ideas in this passage mainly organized?
A) By comparing China and Italy
B) In time order, following events as they happened
C) By describing a problem and its solution
D) By listing reasons people doubted Marco Polo
items.answer: B) In time order, following events as they happened

steps: Look at how the passage moves from one idea to the next.
The passage gives dates and steps in sequence, from leaving Italy in 1271 to returning in 1295, so it is organized in chronological time order, choice B.
Choice A is wrong because the passage does not compare the two countries.
Choice C is wrong because no problem and solution is set up.
Choice D names only the final detail, not how the whole passage is organized, which is a common mix-up of a detail with the overall structure.
solution.answer: B) In time order, following events as they happened

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

The city's new skate park opened last weekend. It covers about half an acre and includes ramps, rails, and a large bowl for more experienced skaters. The park is open from sunrise to sunset and is free for anyone to use. If you ask me, it is by far the best thing the city has ever built, and every kid in town should be there every single day.

Which statement from the passage is an opinion rather than a fact?
A) The skate park opened last weekend.
B) The park covers about half an acre.
C) It is by far the best thing the city has ever built.
D) The park is open from sunrise to sunset.
items.answer: C) It is by far the best thing the city has ever built.

steps: A fact can be checked or proven, while an opinion is a personal judgment that cannot be proven.
Choice C is signaled by "If you ask me" and states a personal judgment that the park is the best thing ever built, which cannot be proven, so it is an opinion.
Choices A, B, and D each give information that could be verified by checking the opening date, measuring the park, or noting its hours, so they are facts.
Mistaking a checkable fact for an opinion, or a value judgment for a fact, is a common error this question tests.
solution.answer: C) It is by far the best thing the city has ever built.

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

For most of human history, people had no fast way to send messages over long distances. A letter might take weeks or even months to cross an ocean by ship. Then, in the 1830s and 1840s, inventors developed the electric telegraph. Operators tapped out coded clicks that traveled along wires almost instantly, and within a few years lines connected distant cities. Soon a cable was even laid across the bottom of the Atlantic Ocean, allowing a message to reach another continent in minutes instead of weeks. The telegraph did not carry the human voice, and the messages it sent were short and plain. Yet it changed how news, business, and even governments worked, because for the first time information could move faster than any ship, train, or rider. In many ways it was the beginning of the connected world we live in today.

Which statement best summarizes the central idea of the passage?
A) The telegraph could not carry the human voice and sent only short, plain messages.
B) A cable was laid across the bottom of the Atlantic Ocean.
C) The telegraph let information travel much faster than ever before and changed how the world communicated.
D) The telegraph was the greatest invention in all of human history.
items.answer: C) The telegraph let information travel much faster than ever before and changed how the world communicated.

steps: A good summary states the main point the whole passage develops, objectively and without adding opinion.

The passage moves from slow old methods to the fast telegraph and stresses that information could finally move faster than any ship, changing news, business, and government, so choice C captures the central idea.
Choice A is a true but narrow detail about the telegraph's limits, not the main point.
Choice B names a single supporting example, the Atlantic cable, which is too narrow to be the summary.
Choice D adds a personal judgment, calling it the greatest invention in history, which the passage never claims and which goes beyond the evidence.
solution.answer: C) The telegraph let information travel much faster than ever before and changed how the world communicated.

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

The Atacama Desert in Chile is one of the driest places on Earth. Some weather stations there have never recorded a single drop of rain. Strangely, this harsh landscape has become a favorite destination for scientists. Because the air is so dry and so few clouds form, the night sky is unusually dark and clear, making it one of the best places in the world to study the stars. The same dryness that keeps almost nothing alive also keeps the air free of the moisture that blurs a telescope's view. Researchers have built some of the world's most powerful observatories high on the desert's ridges. Each clear night, their telescopes capture light from galaxies billions of miles away.

What can the reader most reasonably conclude about why scientists value the Atacama Desert?
A) The desert is so dry that no plants or animals can survive there.
B) The desert's extreme dryness creates dark, clear skies that are ideal for studying the stars.
C) Scientists prefer to work in places where it never rains so they stay dry.
D) The Atacama Desert has the most powerful telescopes that will ever be built.
items.answer: B) The desert's extreme dryness creates dark, clear skies that are ideal for studying the stars.

steps: The question asks for a conclusion that is supported by evidence across the passage.
The passage links the dry air and lack of clouds to a dark, clear night sky and explains this makes it one of the best places to study stars, so choice B is the supported conclusion.
Choice A is a true detail about dryness but does not explain why scientists value the place.
Choice C invents a personal reason about staying dry that the passage never gives, drawing on outside assumption instead of the text.
Choice D overstates the passage by claiming the telescopes are the most powerful that will ever be built, going beyond what the evidence supports.
solution.answer: B) The desert's extreme dryness creates dark, clear skies that are ideal for studying the stars.
